blocks.text: A motorcycle cuts across your path in traffic and, before you have formed a sentence, your heart is pounding, your pupils are wide and your hands tingle. That surge is adrenaline, poured into the blood by the adrenal glands. Later the same day a bunch of plantain in the kitchen turns from green to yellow because another chemical messenger — ethene — is ripening the fruit. Animals and plants both coordinate with hormones; they just use them on very different timescales.

blocks.markdown:
## Endocrine glands and their hormones

A **hormone** is a chemical messenger secreted by an endocrine gland into the blood, which carries it to target organs.

The **pituitary** (beneath the brain) is the master gland. It secretes **ADH** (antidiuretic hormone), which makes the kidney reabsorb water; **growth hormone (GH)**; and **tropic hormones** (TSH, FSH, LH, ACTH) that control other glands.

The **thyroid** in the neck secretes **thyroxine**, which sets the basal metabolic rate. It needs iodine; without iodine the gland swells into a **goitre**.

The **pancreas** (islets of Langerhans) secretes **insulin**, which lowers blood glucose by promoting its uptake and storage as glycogen, and **glucagon**, which raises blood glucose by breaking glycogen down. Shortage of insulin causes **diabetes mellitus**.

The **adrenal** glands secrete **adrenaline**, which prepares the body for emergency action. The **ovary** secretes oestrogen and progesterone; the **testis** secretes testosterone.

blocks.title: Hormone
blocks.text: A chemical substance produced in small amounts by an endocrine gland, transported in the blood, and having a specific effect on one or more target organs. Unlike a nerve impulse, the message is chemical, relatively slow, and can reach every tissue the blood supplies.

blocks.markdown:
## Plant hormones

Plants have no nerves. They coordinate growth with chemicals.

**Auxin** (indoleacetic acid) is made in shoot tips. It causes cell elongation. In **phototropism**, light from one side makes auxin accumulate on the shaded side, so that side grows faster and the shoot bends towards the light. Auxin in the apical bud also suppresses side buds (**apical dominance**); pinch out a tomato tip and the plant bushes.

**Ethene** (ethylene) is a gas that ripens fruit — which is why a ripe plantain in a closed bowl ripens the green ones beside it. Other plant hormones (for completeness) include gibberellins, which elongate stems and help seeds germinate, and cytokinins, which promote cell division.

blocks.title: Classifying two hormone disorders
blocks.prompt: Patient A drinks large volumes of water and produces large volumes of pale urine; blood glucose is normal. Patient B also produces a lot of urine, but the urine contains glucose and blood glucose is high. Name the deficient hormone in each case, the gland, and the disease.

steps.text: Both patients pass a lot of urine, so the first instinct is to say diabetes. The presence or absence of glucose separates the two diseases.
Patient A has normal blood glucose, so insulin is working. The kidney is not reabsorbing water, which is the job of ADH from the pituitary. The disease is diabetes insipidus.
Patient B has glucose in blood and urine, so glucose is not being taken into cells and stored. That is insulin deficiency from the pancreatic islets — diabetes mellitus.
A related trap: a swollen neck with low metabolic rate and iodine-poor diet is thyroxine deficiency (goitre), which is a different gland again.

blocks.answer: A: ADH from the pituitary — diabetes insipidus. B: insulin from the pancreas — diabetes mellitus.

blocks.title: WAEC and JAMB tip
blocks.text: Diabetes mellitus (insulin, pancreas, sugar in urine) is not diabetes insipidus (ADH, pituitary, no sugar in urine). Goitre is iodine and thyroxine, not insulin. For tropisms, auxin collects on the shaded side of a shoot, so the shaded side elongates and the shoot bends towards light — students often reverse this.

points: Endocrine glands secrete hormones into the blood: pituitary (ADH, GH, tropic), thyroid (thyroxine), pancreas (insulin and glucagon), adrenal (adrenaline), ovary and testis.
Nervous coordination is fast, electrical and localised; hormonal coordination is slower, chemical and often widespread.
Insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus; iodine deficiency causes goitre; ADH deficiency causes diabetes insipidus.
Auxin mediates phototropism and apical dominance; ethene ripens fruit.
Adrenaline prepares the body for emergency by raising heart rate and blood glucose.
